title: Compass: interview rubric + welcome flow
content:
Purpose: one-stop practical kit for interviewers + hiring managers + people ops to reduce inconsistency in debriefs and speed early ramp. Combines a compact interviewer rubric, debrief template, candidate experience checklist, and a lightweight 30/60/90 welcome flow managers can re-use.

Status: draft — this is a working doc. Expect small changes after calibration session (week of 2025-08-11).

QUICK NOTES TO SELF:
- Keep behavioral items short for interviewers; focus on decision points.
- We will pilot this with infra & applied-ml hiring lines first.
- Need to sync with Legal on references/offer language for contractors.

1) Interview rubric (single page) — use for all IC and EM technical interviews
- Scoring: 1 (strong no) — 2 (below bar) — 3 (meets bar) — 4 (above bar) — 5 (exceptional)
- Sections and weights (suggested):
  - Technical/role skills (40%) — concrete problem solving, system design, code correctness as applicable
  - Product sense & tradeoffs (20%) — when role touches product or infra tradeoffs
  - Collaboration & communication (15%) — clarity, ability to explain tradeoffs, receiving feedback
  - Ownership & impact (15%) — examples of driving things to production, error handling, postmortems
  - Cultural fit / company values alignment (10%) — curiosity, humility, customer focus

- Calibration tips for interviewers:
  - Use concrete examples: ask for 1–2 specific examples for ownership questions (what, why, outcome, metrics).
  - For coding: prefer open-ended prompts that require reasoning + tests (we use lightweight whiteboard or shared editor).
  - For systems design: define constraints up-front (latency, cost, traffic pattern) — watch for considerations for fallback and degradation (we care about graceful degradation).

- Example short behavioral prompts (pick 2, 12–15 minutes total):
  - Tell me about a time you shipped a feature with imperfect data. How did you decide to proceed?
  - Describe an incident you led. What did you do post-incident?
  - Give an example of a time you disagreed with a stakeholder. How did you resolve it?

- Example technical prompts (choose one depending on level):
  - IC (mid-senior): implement a deduplicated streaming ingestion sketch; focus on correctness and edge cases.
  - Staff/Principal: design a cache-KV service that supports prefix eviction and multi-tenant isolation under burst. Discuss routing/fallback and monitoring.

2) Debrief template (what interviewers fill in within 24 hours)
- Candidate name:
- Role & level applied for:
- Interviewer:
- Date/time:
- Score (1–5) per rubric section (technical, product, collab, ownership, values): list numeric + 1-sentence justification each
- Top 2 strengths (bullets)
- Top 2 concerns / risk areas (bullets)
- Recommendation (hire / no-hire / hire-with-reservations) + suggested level
- Notes for hiring manager (e.g., reasonable salary band expectations, visa/work authorization flags, notice period)

3) Candidate experience checklist (pre-offer) — people ops + recruiter responsibilities
- Pre-screen -> calendar: confirm timezone and accessibility needs
- Interview pack sent 48h before: one-pager about team, tech stack, interviewers + expected topics
- Pre-boarding doc sent on loop completion: benefits summary, NDA + paperwork link, mentor/buddy assigned
- Interview day: ensure buffer between interviews for candidate breathing time; provide interviewer contact (recruiter)
- After interviews: recruiters send next steps timeline within 24h regardless of decision

4) Quick pre-boarding / first-week tasks (owner: people ops + hiring mgr)
- Before Day 1 (T-3 days):
  - IT ticket created for laptop, accounts (git, internal infra, email, slack, VPN) — assignee: infra-team onboarding queue
  - Access requests: Jira, Confluence, analytics, AWS/GCP project enrollment, KMS read-only where needed
  - Manager: confirm first-week calendar and 1:1 cadence
  - Buddy assigned + intro email drafted
- Day 1 schedule (sample):
  - 09:00 — Welcome & HR intro (benefits, payroll, policies)
  - 10:00 — Team welcome: quick round-robin, org context (30 min), mission + current priorities
  - 11:00 — Tech setup shadow (buddy) + dev environment checklist
  - 12:30 — Lunch w/ buddy (optional)
  - 14:00 — Manager 1:1: expectations, immediate 30/60 goals, communication norms
  - 15:00 — Security training & required readings
  - 16:00 — Quick task assignment: small first PR or doc to review (owned by buddy)

- Week 1 focus:
  - Small contributor task shipped (PR merged or doc written)
  - Meeting cadence established
  - Access validated, logging access and SSO checks done
  - 1:1 with manager scheduled weekly for first 90 days

5) Manager's lightweight 30/60/90 template (copyable)
- 30 days (learn & observe):
  - Understand codebase & infra relevant to role (list top 3 areas)
  - Complete small onboarding ticket and get first PR merged
  - Meet key cross-functional partners (CS/infra/product)
- 60 days (contribute & extend):
  - Deliver feature or infra improvement with measurable outcome (latency reduction, flakiness reduced, cost per token improvements)
  - Lead a retrospective / postmortem on a small rollout or experiment
- 90 days (drive & own):
  - Own a medium-sized project end-to-end; set roadmap micro-goals with stakeholders
  - Propose a measurable optimization or reliability improvement and begin execution

6) Buddy program (practical)
- Buddy responsibilities (first 30 days):
  - Daily async check-ins first week, then 2x weekly for weeks 2–4
  - Make sure dev environment works; help with first PR + review cycle
  - Introduce to informal norms and key Slack channels
- Buddy script (first message sample):
  - "Hi X — I’m your buddy, I’ll help with setup and get you into the right channels. My calendar is here [link]. First task: let's get your dev box running — bring any Qs."

7) Risk matrix / rollback signals for early ramp
- Red flags: repeated inability to complete small tasks after 3 iterations, poor communication that leads to missed deadlines, security lapses in access handling
- Yellow flags: slow ramp but good learning attitude, deliverables needing more review than average — propose structured checkpoints every 2 weeks

8) Interviewer calibration checklist (for calibration meeting)
- Bring 3 recent debriefs where you recommended hire/no-hire
- Compare at least one candidate from this rubric to a past hire at same level
- Discuss one edge case where domain knowledge biases the score and how to normalize

9) Templates (copy/paste)
- Debrief quick: "Score: 3/4/3/4/3 — Strengths: system design depth, ownership; Concerns: limited infra benchmarks. Recommendation: hire-with-reservations at L4."
- Offer follow-up: short acceptance email + next steps (people ops fills in start date, equipment, paperwork links)

10) Open questions / TODOs
- Need a light translator guide for non-technical interviewers participating in engineering bar-reads
- Decide on final weights for values vs skills for leadership roles (EM+)
- Confirm where contract hiring differs in scoring and ramp expectations

Attachments & references: link recruiter playbook, Offer templates, legal checklist (internal links in linked_artifacts).

End — please leave comments inline. Next: run pilot with two teams and collect feedback (metric: time-to-offer and first-PR-merged within 30 days).
